reviewer: independent model reviewer (mrev1_k2), did not build the generator
fixes: Top-to-side step (gen_stepping_stone.py rings R3 -> R4): R4 top shoulder is inset to 0.82 R at z = t + dome while R3 sits at 0.985 R and z = 0.85 t, so the top sits on a visible ledge about 0.16 R wide. The canonical shows it as a split block. Change R4 to >= 0.94 R and R3 to z = 0.9 t so the top flows into the side as one convex profile. Target: no horizontal ledge wider than 0.02 m in the profile.

Stone is too thick and too uniform for the concept, where the stones sit just under the water and read as thin, lobed pebbles. Default thickness seeded range 0.15-0.165 m (max 0.30) should become about 0.10-0.13 m, and the 0.15 m minimum should go. Keep plan diameter 0.52-0.58 m.

Outline is nearly round. Default ovality is seeded 0-0.08 and the three-lobe term is weak, so seeds 2 and 3 look like discs. Concept outlines are irregular. Raise default ovality to 0.06-0.12 and add a second wobble term of 0.03-0.05 R so about one stone in three is clearly non-round.

LOD3 (12 tris, hexagonal bipyramid, gen RINGS[3] = R0, R2, R5) reads as a faceted gem or lozenge in the 3/4 sheet, not as a flat stone, and at 36 m it is a 1-2 px dash. Replace it with a flat hexagonal disc: 6 side quads (12 tris) plus a 4-tri fan top, so 16 tris. Ask the lead to raise the LOD3 budget from 12 to 16, or accept 13 with a pentagonal disc. Target: width-to-height at least 4:1 with a flat top.
LOD2 (40 tris) also reads as a diamond at 3/4 because the top ring tapers to a point. Keep R4 at >= 0.9 R so the top stays a disc and the LOD2 silhouette matches LOD0. This is cheap: no added tris.
library_issues: basalt_wet top and chipped rim show bright speckled highlights in the canonical that read as salt or chrome flecks rather than wet basalt. Check the basalt_wet roughness and normal map.
stepping_stone side material is lighter and more grey than the wet top, so the stone reads as two stones glued together. Consider a darker side tone matching the concept.
summary: Recognisable as a flat stone disc at LOD0 and LOD1, and the material split (wet top, basalt side) is the right idea. It falls short on construction: a visible top-to-side ledge makes it read as a stacked block, the stones are too thick and too round compared with the concept, and LOD2/LOD3 turn into diamond or gem shapes that are not nameable at phone size. The first two fixes are generator-only and cheap; the LOD3 fix needs a 4-tri budget increase.
